_comment: NFL trading bot v1. ONE bot, medium risk, PRE-GAME ONLY, PAPER fills. Every tuned number lives here; feature code reads it and hardcodes nothing. Edits apply on the next tick (config is re-read each loop).

data._comment: startSeason gates EVERY historical read. 2025 = user decision: game-to-game matchups older than that are considered stale. NOTE this leaves ~317 games to fit 4 factor weights, so CLV error bars will be wide -- treat early results as directional. replacementBaselineStartSeason is split out because what a backup QB costs you is stable across eras; widen it alone if the injury factor looks noisy.

model._comment: RESIDUAL model. The market price is the ANCHOR, not a weighted factor -- blending p_market as a factor alongside team strength would double-count, because the market price already contains team strength. The model forecasts only the DEVIATION from the market. deltaCap is therefore the real 'how much may the bot disagree with the public' knob.

momentum._comment: Opponent-adjusted EPA/play, exponentially recency-weighted. halfLifeGames=4 means a game 4 weeks ago counts half as much as last week. shrinkGames damps teams with few games on record (week 1-3 of a season).

matchup._comment: The pace x defense INTERACTION. Two fast offenses produce more plays, so defensive EPA/play is applied more times and mechanically matters more in that game -- Lions/Bills. leagueAvgPlays is the normaliser; paceAmplification scales how hard extra plays tilt weight toward defence.

injury._comment: BASELINED, not raw player value. Penalty = player marginal value x (1 - demonstrated replacement quality). The Rams played exactly ONE 2025 game without Nacua, so 'they cope fine' rests on a single game -- shrinkGamesWithout forces that estimate back toward league-average positional replacement until the sample earns its way out. Without this the bot chases noise every week.

situational._comment: Slowest factors for casual money to price. Values are probability points applied to the HOME side. Weather only applies when roof is outdoors/open.

confidence._comment: Scales delta down when inputs are thin (early season, missing injury report, stale book). A low-confidence game is skipped rather than traded small.

risk._comment: Inputs to the DERIVED risk tier (src/accounting/riskTier.js). The tier itself is not set here -- a bot that could name its own tier could label itself anything, so the bands live in the module.
risk._comment_correlation: concurrentCorrelation is the correlation between positions held AT THE SAME TIME. Measured at -0.007 for NFL totals within a week over 2022-2026, i.e. none: games do not share a scoring environment in any detectable way, which was the opposite of what was expected. Clamped to 0 here. A PROPS bot must raise this -- same-game legs key off one game script, and at rho 0.6 with 5 legs the volatility is 1.86x the independent case, so leaving it at 0 would badly understate one.
risk._comment_rounds: How many times the book realistically recycles in a week. Used ONLY in the fallback, before there is enough history to measure turnover directly. NFL is 1 -- one slate, positions held through it. An NBA/NHL/EPL bot MUST raise this (4-6): the weekly cap is CONCURRENT exposure, so a bot recycling the same 25% daily carries far more through the week and would otherwise be rated as though it traded once.

_comment_display: marketScopeLabel and description are written to bots.bot by ensureBot. They lived only in the live database before -- set once by a manual UPDATE -- which is how the card ended up saying 'at medium risk' months after riskTier was recomputed to low. A tier stated in prose goes stale silently; the chip beside the name is derived and cannot.
description: A proprietary BlockPools prediction model focused on NFL game markets. It prices every game against its own estimate of fair value, and trades only where the market disagrees enough to be worth acting on.

policy._comment_slippage: maxSlippageCents, not bps, on purpose: these books tick in whole cents, so at a 0.30 price ONE tick is already 333bps. A percentage cap silently prevents the filler from ever walking past the top level, which looks like a tight risk control and is actually a broken one. Cents are the natural unit of an absolute-tick market.
policy._comment_window: 24h. The day before the game: Friday's final injury report is filed, Saturday adds the weather forecast that actually verifies, and nothing before that is information the model can price. Was 192h, which let it open Week 4 positions 136 hours out.
policy._comment_inplay: The resting sell is NOT cancelled at kickoff -- the bot sets a price it wants and rides the position until that price trades or the market resolves. In play the model has no live feed, so p_fair is stale and is deliberately NOT the basis for the target; instead the order sits at entry + exitInPlayExtraCents (floored at whatever it was resting at pre-kickoff), which is a deliberately ambitious price. That is the point: in-play swings are large enough to reach a level that would never print before kickoff. Holding adds no downside the bot did not already have, since the alternative was riding to settlement anyway -- it only adds the chance of being paid on a swing.
policy._comment_exit: exitAtFairValue rests a SELL at p_fair after each buy. Same expected value as holding to settlement but far lower variance, and it frees capital; if the market never reaches it the position rides to settlement exactly as before, so it is a free option. exitBufferCents sits just under fair so the order is marketable on arrival. The resting price is RE-PRICED every tick as p_fair moves -- a static limit goes stale when an injury shifts fair.
policy._comment: MEDIUM tier. Pre-game only -- no in-play, because there is no live drive-level feed wired and in-play without one is guessing. The bot is meant to SKIP most games: edge must clear the threshold AND the book must be liquid enough to fill.
policy._comment_minEdge: 0.015, lowered from 0.025 on 2026-10-02. The threshold was never calibrated to THIS bot's edge distribution -- it was Argo-7's number. Measured over 17 games Adam-7 actually evaluated in-window: median best edge 0.0145, p90 0.0232, MAXIMUM EVER 0.0287. A 0.025 bar therefore sat at roughly the 93rd percentile of its own output and let through 2 games; Argo-7, whose median edge is 0.0800, clears the same bar on 10 of 11. Same constant, two completely different levels of selectivity. At 0.015 Adam-7 would have taken 7 of 17 (41%), at 0.020 four (24%). Raise it back if the added trades underperform the two it was already taking -- the fitting warns no factor cleared 2 sigma, so these are small edges on an uncalibrated model.
policy._comment_sizing: FLAT, not Kelly, as of week 4. Kelly puts the most money where the edge estimate is largest, which is correct only if that estimate is calibrated -- and week 3 says it is not: the second-largest edge (PHI@CHI, 13.3c) lost 100% while the largest (MIN@TB, 16.0c) won, and the smallest loser and a small winner sat a fraction of a cent apart. Same 2,500 deployed flat would have lost 34 instead of 117. One week proves nothing on its own, but the fitting already said the same thing -- no factor cleared 2 sigma at n=300 -- and sizing off an unranked edge just converts estimation error into position size. Set sizingMode back to kelly when top-quartile-edge trades demonstrably beat bottom-quartile over a real sample.
policy._comment_slippage_cap: 0.01, HALVED alongside minEdge and not optional. edge is measured against best_ask (policy/medium.js), so slippage is spent AFTER the edge test passes: at minEdge 0.015 with 0.02 of permitted slippage the bot could fill a 1.5c edge at -0.5c and never record a complaint. Measured fills say 0.01 costs nothing -- 8 of 10 filled exactly at top of book, worst walk 0.0082.

paper._comment: Paper fills walk the recorded book: consume ask levels until the order is filled, average the price, and record any unfilled remainder honestly. Polymarket's ~$1 minimum order is why cent-sized real orders are not an option -- size here is notional, and the same sizing math carries over unchanged when mode flips to live.

ingest._comment: bookPollSeconds is the depth recorder cadence. Historical book depth cannot be backfilled from anywhere, so this job must run continuously from day one. recordWindowHours is deliberately MUCH wider than policy.openWindowHoursBeforeKickoff: we record every book we can reach, but only trade inside the tighter window. Recording is free and unrepeatable; trading early is neither.
ingest._comment_footprint: STORAGE. Measured 2026-09-27: sports.odds_history had reached 448 MB of a 782 MB database, 57% of everything, on a 500 MB plan -- 195,662 rows and 129 MB in a single day once the totals recorder joined the moneyline one, against 34 rows the day before. Three changes, none of which reduce what the bot can see: bookHeartbeatSeconds makes an unchanged book cost one row per 10 minutes instead of ten (42% of consecutive snapshots were byte-identical); bookLevelsStored 10 -> 5 roughly halves the row, and 5 levels is far more than a $500 position can walk; totalsLinesRecordedPerGame 3 -> 1 records only the line actually traded. The neighbouring lines were kept for a future version that does not exist yet, at triple the cost of the one that does.
ingest._comment_dedup: bookCompareLevels/bookSizeTolerancePct make the change test DECISION-lossless rather than byte-lossless. Measured live: top-of-book was unchanged on 98.1% of polls while the full ladder matched on only 10.5% -- market makers shuffle size at depth on 87.6% of polls without the price moving. A byte compare writes a row for every wobble, which is why the first attempt at this left the daily volume unchanged. Prices must match exactly; sizes may drift 10%; only the top 4 levels count, because exec/paper.js stops at maxSlippageCents and a level a 00 order can never reach cannot change its fill.
ingest._comment_cadence: farPollSeconds samples a game more than midWindowHours away every 10 minutes instead of every 60s. 38 of 158 tracked tokens were for games over 48h out and were polled as often as one kicking off within the hour. Anything at or past kickoff is always polled: that is when the exits ride and the closing line is struck.

_comment_riskTier: riskTier below is a SEED only. run/risk-tier.js derives the live value from the sizing policy and the prices actually traded, and writes bots.bot.risk_tier. Editing it here does not change what users see.
